newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon to ask consultative group for $5 bln.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon to ask consultative group for $5 bln.

text.p: Lebanon will ask a consultative group of nations being formed to help finance its reconstruction for $5 billion over five years in donations and soft loans, acting finance minister Fouad Siniora said on Thursday.

The group, set up in April under a ceasefire understanding that ended a 17-day Israeli blitz against Lebanon, will hold its first meeting in Washington on October 18, Siniora told Reuters in a telephone interview.
It is being organised by the United States, which brokered the ceasefire understanding and includes France, the European Union and Russia and other interested countries.

Siniora said he was sure Japan would attend and there were very good indications that Malaysia and South Korea would also come to the meeting. Lebanon has expressed interest in the participation of the three Asian countries.

Asked what requests Lebanon would present to the group, Siniora said: "We have prepared quite a good number of projects for which we hope we will be able to get assistance, partly in donations and partly in soft loans.
"The amount would reach about $5 billion over five years," he added.
